title: Install AWX on k3s with the AWX Operator
preflight: Windows hypervisor is OFF (bcdedit /set hypervisorlaunchtype off, then reboot). VirtualBox shows the blue V icon, not the green turtle
VM snapshot restored: fresh CentOS Stream 10, booted, logged in as root, 4 vCPU / 8 GB / 60 GB, NIC 1 host-only, NIC 2 NAT
Terminal font large (18 pt or more), dark theme, window about 1280x720 so it is readable at 1080p
Notifications off, no personal tabs or bookmarks visible, desktop clean
Run sheet (ep02/README.md) open on a second screen. Share ONLY the VM or terminal window, not this studio
Mic check done (Live mode) or Silent mode chosen (narration added later with the cloned voice)

steps.title: Open
steps.show: Terminal on the fresh VM, empty prompt. Optional: GitHub repo page ep02 folder.
steps.say: Today we install AWX the way the project recommends: with the AWX Operator on Kubernetes. We use k3s, a one-command Kubernetes, on a single VM. By the end you log in to your own AWX, and I show you three problems I hit so you do not lose a night to them.

steps.title: VM settings and the hypervisor
steps.show: VirtualBox: VM Settings > System (4 CPU, 8 GB), Storage (60 GB), Network (adapter 1 host-only, adapter 2 NAT). Then PowerShell on Windows.
steps.say: 4 vCPU, 8 GB RAM, 60 GB disk. Adapter 1 is host-only so your PC can reach AWX, adapter 2 is NAT for internet. On Windows turn the hypervisor off first: with it on VirtualBox runs in Hyper-V mode, you see a green turtle icon, and my guest crashed.
steps.watch: Show the blue V icon in the VM status bar, not the green turtle.

steps.title: Check the machine
steps.say: Minimums are 2 CPUs, 4 GB free RAM, 15 GB free disk. Read your own numbers out loud.

steps.title: Firewall and SELinux
steps.show: Terminal. Run the block; if firewalld is off, say so and move on.
steps.say: 6443 is the Kubernetes API, 30080 is where AWX will listen, the two 10.x ranges are the pod and service networks. Permissive SELinux is a lab shortcut; production uses the k3s SELinux policy.

steps.title: Install k3s
steps.show: Terminal. Install runs about a minute.
steps.say: k3s is a full Kubernetes in one binary. One flag skips the SELinux RPM, one makes the kubeconfig readable. Wait until the node shows Ready.
steps.watch: Pause on the node line showing Ready. Zoom here.

steps.title: AWX Operator
steps.show: Terminal. Clone the repo, show kustomization.yaml, point at the kube-rbac-proxy override.
steps.say: An operator is a controller that installs AWX from a short YAML and keeps it healthy. Point at the kube-rbac-proxy override: the old gcr.io image is gone, and without this line the operator never starts. Trap number one.
steps.watch: Use Callout: 'Trap 1: old gcr.io image removed' when the cursor is on the override.

steps.title: AWX instance
steps.say: A few lines describe the whole AWX: a name and a NodePort on 30080. The operator does the rest.

steps.title: Watch the pods
steps.show: Terminal. Leave the watch running. About 10 minutes, mostly image downloads.
steps.say: Name each pod as it appears: postgres is the database, web is the UI and API, migration builds the schema, task runs your jobs.
steps.watch: Press Speed when the waiting starts, Speed again when awx-task is Running. If something fails, press Retake and explain, that is good content.

steps.title: Password and login
steps.show: Terminal for the password, then the browser at http://<VM IP>:30080.
cmd: k3s kubectl -n awx get secret awx-admin-password -o jsonpath='{.data.password}' | base64 -d; echo
steps.say: Log in as admin, then change the password right away: user menu, Edit. Do not show the password on screen: blur or cut that frame.
steps.watch: Press Cut around the moment the password is visible, or change it first and show the old value only in the terminal for a second.

steps.title: The three traps
steps.show: ep02/README.md troubleshooting table on GitHub, or the terminal.
steps.say: One: Hyper-V mode crashes the VM, turn the Windows hypervisor off and reboot. Two: the dead gcr.io image, use the images override in kustomization.yaml. Three: images corrupted by a crash, k3s crictl rmi the image and let it pull again.

steps.title: Close
steps.show: VirtualBox: take a snapshot named awx-ready. Then the repo page.
steps.say: That is a working AWX on k3s. Take a snapshot of your VM now, we reuse this lab in every episode. Next time: the eight building blocks of AWX. All commands are in the repo, in the ep02 folder.
